I can't give you a line-by-line account of my internal reasoning, but I can be exact about what was in the request and where my reading came in.

What was supplied: the source record (Weeks's quote, original day 2026-07-01, tier party_statement, category T7), the full Fox News article, six other_source_records (item:e1, e2, e4, e5, e6, e7), empty questions_to_consider, empty stored_pieces and catalog, and research_scope limited to NVDA. The instructions said to classify against every stored piece of linked questions, and there were none.

What I did with that: the NVIDIA-Corning items (e2, e5, e6) are in the request as other_source_records, not in the incoming record. I should not have written that they "appear only in separate Fox News items and are not part of this record." That sentence was my interpretation, and it was an imprecise one. The better statement is that the incoming record itself does not carry the three-facility, 3,000-job, or tenfold-capacity claims, and those came in as separate records that I did not classify, because the task was to process the one source record against stored questions.

I also did not reject any two statements from the request as such. The choice of background_only rested on my judgement that the Weeks quote has no defined metric, no stated period beyond "the coming years," and no NVDA-specific figure. That judgement is mine, not a rule the request stated. If you want the other six records processed, they need their own pass.
